news.title: Daily Brief 2026-07-30: FBI IC3 Impersonation Scam Alert + HaveIBeenPwned Breach Check

news.title: FBI Warns: Scammers Impersonating IC3 to Re-Victimize You
news.excerpt: Scammers Are Pretending to Be the FBI's Internet Crime Center to Steal From You — Again. You get a message: "We recovered your stolen money. Click here to claim it." The sender claims to be from the IC3 — the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center. They might even have an AI-generated video of an FBI official "confirming" it's real. It's a lie. The IC3 never contacts victims through social media, email, or phone. They never recover funds for you. They never ask for payment to release money. This is a re-victimization scam targeting people who've already been scammed once. What to do: Type www.ic3.gov directly into your browser — never click a link. If someone says they're from IC3 and wants money or info, it's a scam. Report it at the real IC3 site. *Source: FBI IC3 PSA — July 2026*

news.title: FTC Warns: Fake CAPTCHA Scams Hijack Your Computer
news.excerpt: Scammers use fake CAPTCHAs that tell you to press Windows+R, paste, and Enter — this runs malicious code. Real CAPTCHAs never ask for keyboard commands. Close the tab immediately if a verification asks you to open Run or paste anything.

posts.title: Find any file instantly — Everything Search indexes your whole drive in seconds at voidtools.com
posts.summary: Everything by voidtools is a tiny free program that indexes every filename on your Windows drive in about one second and shows results as you type. Download the installer at voidtools.com (choose 64-bit for modern PCs).
posts.truth: Windows Search is slow because it reads file contents, not just names. Everything only reads the file table — it's the difference between reading every book in the library versus just checking the card catalog. Customers tell me "I can never find my stuff" and five minutes later they're typing "tax 2024" and seeing the PDF instantly.

posts.title: Microsoft Edge July 2026 security update patches 7 critical flaws — update at edge://settings/help
posts.summary: Microsoft Edge 150.0.4078.83 fixes seven vulnerabilities including remote code execution bugs. Open Edge, go to edge://settings/help and it will check and install automatically.
posts.truth: I see this all the time — customers come in with a "slow computer" and it's actually a browser that hasn't been patched in months. The bad guys know most people ignore browser updates. Edge updates itself in the background, but only if you let it. Closing and reopening Edge once a week is the easiest security habit you can build.

posts.title: Microsoft Windows July 2026 Patch Tuesday Fixes Record 570 Vulnerabilities Including 3 Zero-Days
posts.summary: Microsoft released its largest Patch Tuesday ever on July 14, 2026, patching 570 vulnerabilities across Windows, Office, SharePoint, Exchange, and Azure. Two zero-days were actively exploited: CVE-2026-56155 (AD FS elevation of privilege) and CVE-2026-56164 (SharePoint Server authentication bypass). A third, CVE-2026-50661 (BitLocker bypass with physical access), was publicly disclosed. Critical RCEs include CVE-2026-58644 (SharePoint), CVE-2026-58608 (Print Spooler), and CVE-2026-58631 (Windows Admin Center). Obtain via Windows Update (Settings > Update & Security) or Microsoft Update Catalog (catalog.update.microsoft.com). Enterprises should prioritize AD FS, SharePoint, and internet-facing servers immediately.
posts.truth: Microsoft July 2026 Patch Tuesday released July 14, 2026 per MSRC release notes; 570 CVEs confirmed via Microsoft Security Update Guide. Two exploited zero-days (CVE-2026-56155, CVE-2026-56164) confirmed in Microsoft Security Response Center blog and CISA KEV catalog. CVE-2026-50661 BitLocker bypass publicly disclosed. Critical RCE CVEs listed in official advisory.

posts.title: Firefox adds HDR video, QR code sharing, and PDF merging — free at firefox.com
posts.summary: Firefox (released July 21, 2026) adds HDR video playback on Windows, QR code sharing from any page (right-click → Share → Generate QR Code), and drag-and-drop PDF merging in the built-in PDF editor. Download free at firefox.com or update via Menu → Help → About Firefox.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize their browser can do more than show web pages. Firefox's PDF editor now lets you combine multiple PDFs by dragging one into the sidebar of another — no Adobe Acrobat subscription needed. The QR code trick is handy for sending a page from your computer to your phone without emailing yourself. And HDR video means movies and YouTube actually look right on an HDR screen. Download free at firefox.com or update via Menu → Help → About Firefox.

posts.title: Florida lightning kills electronics — an APC SurgeArrest power strip stops the surge for $30 at Home Depot or Lowes
posts.summary: Florida leads the nation in lightning strikes. A real surge protector (not a power strip) like the APC SurgeArrest P11U2 or P12U2 gives you 11–12 protected outlets, 2 USB ports, and a $300,000 connected-equipment warranty. Buy at Home Depot, Lowes, or Amazon — look for "SurgeArrest" on the box.
posts.truth: I've replaced more motherboards fried by lightning than I can count. The $10 power strip from the drugstore has a light that glows but zero protection — it's just an extension cord with a switch. A real surge protector has a joule rating (look for 2,000+) and a warranty that pays for your gear if it fails. In Lake City, that's not optional.

posts.title: Stop the trackers following you — Privacy Badger learns and blocks them free at privacybadger.org
posts.summary: Privacy Badger is a free browser extension from the Electronic Frontier Foundation that automatically learns which companies are tracking you across sites and blocks them. Install it at privacybadger.org (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Opera).
posts.truth: Most people don't realize that when they visit a news site, a recipe blog, and their bank in the same hour, a dozen invisible companies just stitched together a profile of everything they did. Privacy Badger doesn't need you to configure lists or rules — it watches behavior and blocks the trackers that act sneaky. Install once, forget it.

posts.title: Tip: Check Have I Been Pwned (haveibeenpwned.com) for June 2026 Stealer Logs Breach (56M Emails, 124M Passwords)
posts.summary: The June 2026 Stealer Logs breach added 56 million unique email addresses and 124 million unique passwords to Have I Been Pwned on June 15, 2026. Stealer logs capture credentials from infostealer malware — meaning passwords were actively stolen from infected machines, not just leaked from a database. Visit haveibeenpwned.com, enter your email, and check the 'Stealer Logs' section of your dashboard. If found: immediately change that password everywhere you reused it, enable 2FA on all affected accounts, and use a password manager (1Password, Bitwarden) to generate unique passwords. Obtain method: Free web lookup at haveibeenpwned.com or domain monitoring via HIBP API v3.
posts.truth: Have I Been Pwned added June 2026 Stealer Logs breach on June 15, 2026 per HIBP breach page. 56M unique emails and 124M unique passwords confirmed in breach overview. Stealer logs indicate active malware credential theft per HIBP FAQ. Free email lookup and Pwned Passwords search available at haveibeenpwned.com. Domain monitoring via HIBP API v3.

posts.title: Run your own private AI chatbot offline free — Jan.ai installs in minutes at jan.ai
posts.summary: Jan.ai is a free, open-source app that runs AI models entirely on your PC — no internet, no account, no data leaves your machine. Download at jan.ai or github.com/janhq/jan/releases. Needs 8 GB+ RAM; works on Windows, Mac, and Linux.
posts.truth: I get asked about AI all the time. People want to try it but don't want their questions sent to some company's server. Jan.ai solves that — it downloads a model and runs it locally. Your chats stay on your computer. It's not as polished as ChatGPT, but for drafting emails, summarizing PDFs, or brainstorming, it's genuinely useful and costs nothing.
